                    ### Question
                    A 32-year-old woman comes to her doctor’s office with abdominal distention, diffuse abdominal pain, and a history of 10–12 bowel movements a day for the last week. She was diagnosed with Crohn’s disease 3 years ago. Today, vitals are normal. Her abdomen is mildly distended and diffusely tender to palpation. A CT scan shows evidence of a fistula and strictures located in the last 30 cm of her ileum. A resection of the affected portion of the bowel is scheduled. What changes in bile metabolism are expected in this patient post-procedure?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Absorption of vitamin K will not be impaired
opb. Synthesis of cholesterol in the liver will decrease
opc. The balance of the components in bile will be altered
opd. Enteric bacteria will remain the same in the small intestine
ope. Absorption of  7⍺-dehydroxylated bile will decrease

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
After ileal resection, the reabsorption of bile acids is decreased due to the loss of the ileum, which is the primary site for bile acid reabsorption. This leads to increased bile acid loss and altered bile composition, supporting option opc. The liver compensates by increasing bile acid synthesis, which can alter cholesterol metabolism, but this does not directly support option opb as a decrease in cholesterol synthesis is not a consensus outcome. The decreased enterohepatic circulation of bile acids can impair the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, including vitamin K, contradicting option opa. The increased presence of bile acids in the colon can alter gut microbiota, suggesting a potential change in enteric bacteria, which contradicts option opd. The reabsorption of 7⍺-dehydroxylated bile acids is decreased, supporting option ope. The retrieved evidence path regarding vitamin K is too broad and does not directly clarify the specific impact of ileal resection on vitamin K absorption. Therefore, the most consensus-aligned changes in bile metabolism post-procedure are altered bile composition and decreased reabsorption of 7⍺-dehydroxylated bile acids.
